newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks creep up, rally to continue.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks creep up, rally to continue.

text.p: Most Croatian stocks closed higher on Wednesday in slightly more modest trade, but market players expected a surprise summer rally to continue this week.
"Today was a little quieter but not drastically for this time of year," said one trader with a foreign client base.
Overall, eight of 16 issues rose, three fell and five ended flat with volume and turnover shrinking as strong investor interest in some of the blue chips seemed to wane.
Exceptional demand for leading drugs firm Pliva propelled its price up 10 kuna to a new historic high of 571. It sold 5,520 shares and was the day's most active issue.
Unusually strong buying for the holiday season was prompted two weeks ago by a Zagreb bourse decision to scrap its commission during the summer in an effort to boost liquidity.
Together with the other market heavyweight -- Zagrebacka Banka -- Pliva has since forged ahead, scoring new day-to-day records over the past week.
Both have traced the gains of their London-traded Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs), buoyed by the dollar strength.
Pliva's 1/5 GDRs fetched $17.825 on the London Stock Exchange, compared to Tuesday's $17.525, though receeding from $17.85 at the open.

Zagrebacka's fully-listed ordinary stock closed flat at 2,400 on volume of 145 after peaking at a 2,447-kuna all-time high during the session after its 1/10 GDRs rose to $37.75 from $37.25 each on London's Seaq.

"Both (Pliva and Zagrebacka) still have room for a slight further growth. And if their first-half results prove to be as good as rumoured, their prices could rise again in the autumn," said Denis Fuduric of IB Austria brokerage.
The bank's preferred E-series, up 38 kuna or 2.53 percent to 1,540 kuna on volume of 420, led Wednesday's gainers.
Biggest decliner was fully-listed ship repairer Viktor Lenac, losing 11 kuna or 6.36 percent to 162 kuna with 145 shares sold.

It made a debut at 116 kuna on July 16, making steady gains to end last week at a record 180 kuna. But traded volume has varied daily from zero to several thousand units, signalling a mixed reception among buyers.
"Lenac is a relatively small company and foreign investors are not all that interested in it," Fuduric said. "Like Varazdinska Banka, it rose too strongly almost at once and is now retracting."
Varazdinska's common stock rose 4.10 kuna to 219 on volume of 4,978 units, recovering after recent losses.
